articles.excerpt: La prochaine génération de leaders montréalais en IA en a long à dire sur les risques réels et exagérés de cette technologie. Binding Operational Directive (BOD) 26-04: Prioritizing Security Updates Based on Risk establishes vulnerability management requirements for Federal Civilian Executive Branch (FCEB) agencies. BOD 26-04 reinforces the importance of the KEV Catalog and requires federal agencies to prioritize rapid remediation of high-risk vulnerabilities, specifically those identified by Common Vulnerabilities and Exposures (CVEs) listed in CISA’s KEV Catalog on publicly exposed assets that grant total control of the asset post-exploitation, while deferring action for lower-risk vulnerabilities. BOD 26-04 further establishes basic expectations for when agencies must check whether threat actors compromised the system before the patch was applied. articles.excerpt: Amazon CloudWatch Omni now supports collecting Azure resource logs, Azure Monitor platform metrics, virtual network (VNet) flow logs, and traces from Application Insights. Teams that run workloads on both AWS and Azure no longer need separate monitoring tools or custom pipelines to see their whole environment. Central operations, DevOps, and site reliability engineering (SRE) teams can now view Azure telemetry alongside their AWS telemetry in one place. To get started, connect a Microsoft Entra ID tenant to your AWS account and Region. You can choose the telemetry types, subscriptions, Azure regions, resource types, and tags to collect. Azure telemetry lands in Amazon CloudWatch, and Omni spaces can monitor applications and infrastructure across cloud providers. For example, during an incident you can trace a slow request from an Azure-hosted service to its AWS dependencies without switching consoles. You can set up the connectors in the Amazon CloudWatch Omni console or with the AWS CLI. Azure telemetry collection is available in all Azure Public Regions and can be ingested to all regions where CloudWatch Omni is available. To get started, visit the CloudWatch Omni User Guide and for pricing visit pricing page.
articles.summary: Amazon CloudWatch Omni permet désormais de collecter les journaux de ressources Azure, les métriques de plateforme Azure Monitor, les journaux de flux VNet et les traces Application Insights. Les équipes qui exploitent des charges sur AWS et Azure peuvent ainsi suivre leur environnement complet dans un seul outil, après avoir connecté un tenant Microsoft Entra ID. La collecte est offerte dans toutes les régions publiques d'Azure.
articles.title: Amazon CloudWatch Omni now supports Microsoft Azure platform logs, metrics and traces

articles.excerpt: Web Search on Amazon Bedrock, the tool that grounds AI agents and applications in cited, current web information, now supports five new languages, plus non-US English, on Amazon Bedrock AgentCore and Amazon Bedrock: Spanish, French, German, Italian, and Japanese. Agents serving users in these languages get results that draw on local-language sources. We are also introducing a new optional country field that biases results toward sources from a specific country - just pass an ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 country code, such as “JP” or “DE”. This is useful for agents that serve users in multiple countries, for questions whose answer depends on the user's actual or preferred location (e.g., local regulations, prices or public officials), and for surfacing regional sources. Both the expanded language support and the optional country field are available today in every Region where Web Search is offered: US East (N. Virginia), US East (Ohio), US West (Oregon), Asia Pacific (Sydney), Asia Pacific (Tokyo), and Europe (Ireland) for Web Search on Amazon Bedrock AgentCore, and US Regions for Web Search on Amazon Bedrock. Queries are processed in the Region you call, helping organizations meet data residency requirements. Existing customers get the new language capabilities automatically, with no code changes, and pricing is the same in every language. To get started with Web Search on Amazon Bedrock, checkout the developer guide and the web search product page .
articles.summary: Web Search on Amazon Bedrock prend désormais en charge cinq nouvelles langues (espagnol, français, allemand, italien et japonais) ainsi que l'anglais non américain, sur AgentCore et Bedrock. Un nouveau champ optionnel « country », acceptant un code ISO 3166-1 alpha-2, permet d'orienter les résultats vers les sources d'un pays donné. Les clients existants bénéficient automatiquement de ces nouveautés sans modification de code, au même tarif.
articles.title: Web Search on Amazon Bedrock expands language support and country-aware search

articles.excerpt: Amazon Relational Database Service (Amazon RDS) for Oracle now provides a Primary Endpoint, a DNS name that always resolves to the current primary DB instance in a replica configuration. When you switch over to an Oracle replica, Amazon RDS points the Primary Endpoint to the new primary DB instance, so you don't need to change your application connection strings. Previously, after each switchover, you had to update connection strings or DNS records to point to the new primary DB instance, which often required change approvals and coordination across teams. With Primary Endpoint, you can run planned switchovers, such as disaster recovery drills, to replicas in the same AWS Region or to cross-Region replicas without changing your application configuration. If your applications connect through the Primary Endpoint, you don't need to update their connection strings after the switchover. Every RDS for Oracle Enterprise Edition DB instance has a Primary Endpoint at no additional charge, and you don't have to create it. The Primary Endpoint is provided in addition to the instance endpoint, so your existing applications aren't affected. Primary Endpoint is available in all commercial AWS Regions where Amazon RDS for Oracle is available. To learn more, see Using the Primary Endpoint for Amazon RDS for Oracle in the Amazon RDS User Guide.
articles.summary: Amazon RDS for Oracle propose désormais un « Primary Endpoint », un nom DNS qui pointe toujours vers l'instance principale d'une configuration de réplication. Lors d'une bascule vers une réplique, les chaînes de connexion n'ont plus besoin d'être modifiées, ce qui facilite les exercices de reprise après sinistre, y compris vers des répliques situées dans une autre région. Ce point d'accès est fourni sans frais supplémentaires en plus du point d'accès d'instance existant.
articles.title: Amazon RDS for Oracle now supports Primary Endpoint

articles.excerpt: AWS Lambda now publishes Event Function state change events to Amazon EventBridge . Lambda emits an event each time an Event Function version changes state because of a customer action, such as creating, updating, publishing, or deleting a function. These events help platform and DevOps teams to trigger automation as soon as a function becomes ready to invoke, an update finishes, or an operation fails, without polling the GetFunction API. Customers use Lambda Event Functions to build APIs, event processing workloads, multi-step workflows, and data pipelines. As organizations grow to thousands of functions, platform teams need to know when a function changes state so they can take the next step. For example, a deployment pipeline can run integration tests and then shift alias traffic once a new version becomes active. Until now, these tools had to poll the GetFunction API to track state changes. Polling consumed API quota, slowed down pipelines, and required custom retry logic, which added operational overhead. With this launch, you can create EventBridge rules that match on fields such as the function ARN, detail type, or state, and route matched events to targets such as AWS Step Functions , AWS Lambda, Amazon SNS , or Amazon SQS . This helps you build reliable, event-driven deployment pipelines across all of your functions, without writing or maintaining custom polling logic. This feature is available in all commercial AWS Regions . You can create rules by using the…
articles.summary: AWS Lambda publie désormais des événements de changement d'état des fonctions vers Amazon EventBridge, émis à chaque création, mise à jour, publication ou suppression d'une fonction. Les équipes de plateforme peuvent ainsi déclencher de l'automatisation dès qu'une fonction est prête, qu'une mise à jour se termine ou qu'une opération échoue, sans interroger l'API GetFunction. Les règles EventBridge peuvent filtrer sur l'ARN, le type de détail ou l'état, et router les événements vers Step Functions, Lambda, SNS ou SQS. La fonctionnalité est offerte dans toutes les régions commerciales d'AWS.
articles.title: AWS Lambda now publishes Event Function state change events to Amazon EventBridge

articles.excerpt: AWS Network Firewall announces the public preview of automated Internet firewall, a new centralized control that allows you to configure Network Firewall, with native network address translation (NAT) capability, on the internet gateways of all the Virtual Private Clouds (VPCs) in your environment. Using automated Internet firewall mode, you can centrally define your Network Firewall security rules and enforce them on all inbound and outbound traffic across the internet gateways of your VPCs. You are not required to make routing or architectural changes to deploy automated Internet firewall. You can deploy it across select VPCs or your entire account, organization or organization unit. AWS Network Firewall is a stateful, managed, network firewall and intrusion detection and prevention service for your VPC. Customers use it to inspect their traffic and secure AWS resources. Prior to this launch, customers would configure AWS Network Firewalls inside their VPCs in the traffic path of all internet communication to achieve thorough security coverage against the threats on the internet. They deployed Network Firewall endpoints in dedicated subnets and made route updates for every subnet that needed internet access across all their VPCs. In addition, they monitored the environment to ensure that no new internet network paths bypassed these security controls. Automated Internet firewall makes this deployment and management simpler. You just define and maintain filtering rules, and…
articles.summary: AWS annonce la préversion publique d'un mode « pare-feu Internet automatisé » pour AWS Network Firewall, qui permet de configurer de façon centralisée le pare-feu, avec traduction d'adresses réseau (NAT), sur les passerelles Internet de tous les VPC d'un environnement. Les règles de sécurité définies une seule fois s'appliquent au trafic entrant et sortant de ces VPC, sans modification de routage ou d'architecture, et le déploiement peut cibler certains VPC ou un compte, une organisation ou une unité d'organisation entière. Cette nouveauté simplifie la configuration et la surveillance que les clients devaient jusqu'ici effectuer manuellement sous forme de points de terminaison et de routes par sous-réseau.
articles.title: AWS Network Firewall introduces automated Internet firewall in public preview

articles.excerpt: Amazon Relational Database Service (Amazon RDS) for Oracle now supports Replica First Patching, which reduces downtime during minor version upgrades. Replica First Patching is available for Enterprise Edition DB instances. With Replica First Patching, you apply a minor version upgrade to a replica in the same AWS Region first while your primary DB instance continues to serve traffic, and then switch over to the replica when you're ready to complete the upgrade. If the replica is in read-only mode, you can validate the new minor engine version with your read traffic. Replica First Patching helps you keep mission-critical Oracle workloads current on minor versions with less disruption. You choose when to switch over within the switchover window, for example during a low-traffic period. If you don't switch over within the window, Amazon RDS rolls back the replica to its original minor engine version. After the switchover, Amazon RDS completes the upgrade on the new primary DB instance. Amazon RDS then upgrades your other replicas, including your former primary DB instance, to the same minor engine version. We recommend that you connect your applications through the Primary Endpoint when you use Replica First Patching. The Primary Endpoint is a DNS name that resolves to the current primary DB instance, so your applications reach the new primary DB instance after the switchover without connection string changes. Replica First Patching is available at no additional charge in all…
articles.summary: Amazon RDS for Oracle prend désormais en charge le Replica First Patching, qui réduit les interruptions lors des mises à niveau de version mineure. La mise à niveau s'applique d'abord à un réplica de la même région pendant que l'instance primaire continue de servir le trafic, puis une bascule est effectuée au moment choisi dans la fenêtre de bascule, la fonctionnalité étant offerte pour les instances Enterprise Edition. Si la bascule n'a pas lieu dans la fenêtre, le réplica revient à sa version mineure d'origine.
articles.title: Amazon RDS for Oracle now supports Replica First Patching for reduced downtime

articles.excerpt: Amazon Cognito multi-Region replication (MRR) now supports additional AWS Regions, extending the resilience benefits of MRR to more workloads. Amazon Cognito helps you implement secure sign-in and access control for users, AI agents, and microservices in minutes, and MRR lets you synchronize user and machine identity data, including credentials, user pool configurations, and federation setups, to a secondary user pool in a standby Region you designate in near real-time. With user data in the standby Region, you can redirect traffic and keep authentication available if there is a disruption in your primary Region. Previously, MRR was available in 16 commercial Regions and the AWS GovCloud (US) Regions. You can now also use MRR to replicate your user data to Asia Pacific (Hyderabad, Hong Kong, Jakarta, Malaysia, Melbourne, New Zealand, Osaka, Taipei, Thailand), Canada West (Calgary), Europe (Milan, Spain, Zurich), Israel (Tel Aviv), Mexico (Central), Africa (Cape Town) Regions, helping you meet resilience, data residency, and compliance requirements in the Regions that best align with your needs. MRR is available as an add-on for user pools on the Essentials or Plus feature plans, and requires a multi-Region AWS KMS customer managed key (CMK). For the full list of AWS Regions where Amazon Cognito is available, see AWS Capabilities by Region . To get started, visit the developer guide for instructions and the pricing page for pricing details.
articles.summary: Amazon Cognito élargit sa réplication multi-région (MRR) à de nouvelles régions AWS, dont plusieurs régions Asie-Pacifique, Canada Ouest (Calgary), Europe, Israël, Mexique et Afrique. La MRR synchronise les données d'identité des utilisateurs et des machines vers un pool d'utilisateurs secondaire dans une région de secours, ce qui permet de maintenir l'authentification en cas de perturbation de la région principale. Elle est offerte en option sur les forfaits Essentials ou Plus et exige une clé KMS multi-région gérée par le client.
articles.title: Amazon Cognito extends multi-Region replication to additional AWS Regions

articles.excerpt: Amazon Neptune Serverless now delivers up to 30% better performance at the same price per Neptune Capacity Unit, running on AWS Graviton4 processors. The new Graviton4-based platform also brings an improved scaling algorithm that adjusts Neptune Capacity Units (NCUs) more closely to your workload. This especially helps applications with many concurrent graph queries, such as real-time fraud detection, recommendation engines and generative AI applications that run graph lookups on every request. Neptune Serverless scales database capacity automatically as your application’s demand changes, so you can run graph applications with spiky or unpredictable traffic, such as fraud detection, recommendation engines, and generative AI applications, without provisioning for peak capacity. You pay only for the capacity you use. All newly created Neptune Serverless instances will be using AWS Graviton4 processors. You can create new Neptune Serverless instances using AWS Management Console or the AWS CLI . You can upgrade existing clusters to the latest version in the next release. For more information on pricing and regional availability, refer to the Amazon Neptune pricing page and Neptune Serverless documentation .
articles.summary: Amazon Neptune Serverless annonce jusqu'à 30 % de performance en plus au même prix par unité de capacité Neptune (NCU), grâce aux processeurs AWS Graviton4. La plateforme améliorée inclut un algorithme de mise à l'échelle plus fidèle à la charge de travail, utile notamment pour la détection de fraude en temps réel et les moteurs de recommandation. Les nouvelles instances utilisent Graviton4, et les clusters existants pourront être mis à niveau lors d'une prochaine version.
articles.title: Amazon Neptune Serverless now delivers up to 30% better performance and smarter scaling

articles.excerpt: Amazon CloudWatch now supports a 30-day query window for PromQL queries against OpenTelemetry metrics, up from 7 days. You can query a month of data in a single request, chart month-over-month and week-over-week trends on one dashboard, and alarm on a 30-day baseline. Teams typically define service level objectives (SLOs) over a 30-day rolling window, longer than a 7-day query can measure. You can now calculate availability and remaining error budget for a full SLO period in one query, and alarm when a service is on track to exhaust its budget. A month of history also makes capacity forecasts more reliable, because a 7-day baseline skews to a single busy weekend. This feature is available at no additional cost in all AWS Regions where PromQL queries against OpenTelemetry metrics in Amazon CloudWatch are available. To get started, see Query OpenTelemetry metrics with PromQL in the Amazon CloudWatch User Guide .
articles.summary: Amazon CloudWatch porte à 30 jours la fenêtre de requête PromQL sur les métriques OpenTelemetry, contre 7 jours auparavant. Cela permet de calculer la disponibilité et le budget d'erreur restant sur une période complète de SLO, ainsi que d'alerter si un service risque d'épuiser son budget. La fonctionnalité est offerte sans frais supplémentaire dans toutes les régions où PromQL sur ces métriques est disponible.
articles.title: Amazon CloudWatch extends the PromQL query window to 30 days

articles.excerpt: AWS Partners can now map their target accounts against AWS records and find where to collaborate with AWS on joint go-to-market before an opportunity exists. Account Mapping and Planning in AWS Partner Central replaces manual, spreadsheet-based account mapping. Upload a target account list through CSV, API, or CRM integration, and accounts are matched automatically against AWS records, including accounts without an ACE opportunity and in any country. Partners can use Account Mapping and Planning to enrich matched accounts with AWS Marketplace propensity insights, solution-level purchase likelihood, and eligibility for programs such as the Partner Greenfield Program and the Partner-Led Sales Motion. This helps Partners prioritize high-propensity and program-eligible accounts for go-to-market activity. Eligible Partners can also request joint account planning with AWS sales on accounts marked Qualified, so AWS and Partner teams can align on an account strategy earlier. Account planning is available to Consulting Partners that are ACE-eligible, Premier tier and managed by an AWS Partner Development Manager (PDM), and to ISVs that are ACE-eligible, enrolled in the SaaS Co-sell Benefit program and PDM-managed. Account Mapping and Planning is available under the Sell tab in AWS Partner Central, and account matching and enrichment are open to all ACE-eligible Partners. Partners can work in the Partner Central console, through the API and SDK, through the Partner Central MCP…
articles.summary: AWS Partner Central propose désormais Account Mapping and Planning, qui remplace la cartographie manuelle de comptes cibles dans des tableurs. Les partenaires importent leur liste de comptes (CSV, API ou intégration CRM) pour qu'elle soit associée automatiquement aux données AWS, puis enrichie de signaux de propension et d'admissibilité à des programmes; la planification conjointe avec les ventes AWS est réservée à certains partenaires Consulting et ISV.
articles.title: Account Mapping and Planning now available in AWS Partner Central

articles.excerpt: AWS Partners can now plan, launch, fund, and measure demand generation campaigns in one AI-powered experience. Demand Center in AWS Partner Central succeeds Marketing Central and brings together Marketing Central and MDF capabilities, letting you work in Partner Central, in your CRM, or in your AI agents. Create hero and distribution assets in multiple languages in minutes with AI campaign creation. Generate content from reference materials, a URL, or a description, and launch it across email, social, and banner ads. Upload leads to get them enriched with propensity signals and recommended next actions. Choose from ready-to-run Partner Ready Campaign kits or connect with AWS-vetted agencies through Agency Connect. Generate case studies with AI from ACE closed-won opportunities, and tailor campaign content to the leads included in each campaign. Connect your CRM or marketing automation tool agent-to-agent, or use Demand Center inside agents such as AWS Quick through the Partner Central MCP server. Track campaign-to-revenue performance in Partner Analytics. To get started, sign in to AWS Partner Central and select Demand Center.
articles.summary: AWS a rendu Demand Center disponible dans AWS Partner Central, qui remplace Marketing Central et regroupe ses fonctions avec celles du MDF pour planifier, lancer, financer et mesurer des campagnes de génération de demande. L'outil permet de créer du contenu assisté par IA dans plusieurs langues, de le diffuser par courriel, réseaux sociaux et bannières, et d'enrichir les pistes avec des signaux de propension. Il se connecte aussi à un CRM ou à un outil de marketing automatisé, et le suivi des revenus se fait dans Partner Analytics.
articles.title: Demand Center now available in AWS Partner Central

articles.excerpt: AWS Partners can now organize enriched leads and plan outreach with lead groups and channel recommendations in AWS Partner Central. Enriched leads are automatically grouped by solution area and segmented into sales-ready, marketing-ready, and limited-potential groups, so you no longer have to segment leads by hand. Limited-potential leads help you avoid spending time and budget on leads unlikely to convert, lowering your cost of acquiring new customers. For each enriched lead, you also get guidance on whether phone or email may be more effective, along with AI-generated call scripts and email scripts to act on it. Marketing-ready lead groups can be sent to Demand Center to create assets and launch targeted campaigns. Sales-ready leads can be exported to the Partner's CRM for direct outreach. Lead groups and channel recommendations are available to ACE-eligible Partners on the Leads page in AWS Partner Central and through the AWS Partner Central Selling API. To get started, sign in to AWS Partner Central and go to the Leads page.
articles.summary: AWS Partner Central ajoute des groupes de prospects et des recommandations de canal. Les prospects enrichis sont regroupés automatiquement par domaine de solution et classés en sales-ready, marketing-ready ou potentiel limité, avec des conseils sur le téléphone ou le courriel et des scripts générés par IA. La fonctionnalité est offerte aux partenaires admissibles ACE via la page Leads et l'API Selling.
articles.title: Lead groups and channel recommendations now available in AWS Partner Central

articles.excerpt: Today, Amazon CloudWatch announces built-in monitoring for open source tools running on your Amazon EKS clusters, including Karpenter, KEDA, vLLM, KServe, SGLang, Ray and Knative Serving. You get dashboards for the tools you already use without running Prometheus or Grafana yourself. Monitoring starts automatically when you enable OTel Container Insights. For your AI inference workloads, you can see queued requests, time to first token, and KV cache usage for each model server. For autoscaling, you can see which scalers are failing and how long your scale loop takes. CloudWatch tags every metric with its pod, workload, and node, so you can trace a slow model server to the node it runs on. These EKS solutions are available in version 8.0.0 and later of the add-on and Helm chart, in all AWS Regions where CloudWatch supports OpenTelemetry metrics. Metrics are charged at the Amazon EKS OpenTelemetry ingestion rate of $0.08 per GB. For details, see Amazon CloudWatch insights pricing . To get started, see Solutions in the Amazon CloudWatch User Guide.
articles.summary: Amazon CloudWatch ajoute une surveillance intégrée pour des outils Kubernetes open source sur les clusters EKS, dont Karpenter, KEDA, vLLM, KServe, SGLang, Ray et Knative Serving, sans avoir à gérer Prometheus ou Grafana. Elle démarre automatiquement lorsque OTel Container Insights est activé et offre des tableaux de bord pour les requêtes en file d'attente, le temps jusqu'au premier jeton et l'utilisation du cache KV des serveurs de modèles, ainsi que pour l'état des autoscalers. Ces fonctionnalités sont disponibles dans la version 8.0.0 et ultérieures de l'extension et du chart Helm, au prix de 0,08 $ par Go de métriques ingérées.
articles.title: Amazon CloudWatch EKS Container Insights now offers built-in monitoring for open source Kubernetes tools

articles.excerpt: AWS Quick now supports assignments for custom permissions and limit profiles to groups from your enterprise identity provider (IdP). Administrators can now apply feature restrictions and per-user resource limits to IdP groups, in addition to the existing user, role, and account assignments. Organizations can align governance with their enterprise identity structure without maintaining assignments for individual users. Administrators manage user, account or group assignments in the Quick administration console or through new policy assignment APIs. For example, an organization can assign its finance group a custom permissions profile that blocks members from creating agents, or apply Deny by Default so that, within selected feature categories, the group can use only capabilities an administrator explicitly allows. Administrators can also assign a limit profile to a group to set each member’s index capacity and agent hours. Quick enforces these limits automatically as users consume resources. When group-level assignments apply to a user who belongs to multiple groups, Quick resolves overlapping assignments as follows: for custom permissions, a capability denied by any group stays denied, and for limit profiles, the user receives the highest value for each limit type across those groups. Group assignments are available in Quick for Professional and Enterprise plans. For feature availability by AWS Region, see AWS Quick Regions . To learn more, see the custom permissions and…
articles.summary: AWS Quick permet désormais d'attribuer des profils de permissions personnalisées et des profils de limites à des groupes issus du fournisseur d'identité d'entreprise, en plus des utilisateurs, rôles et comptes. Un utilisateur appartenant à plusieurs groupes reçoit une capacité refusée si un groupe la refuse, et la valeur la plus élevée pour chaque limite. Ces fonctionnalités sont offertes dans les forfaits Professional et Enterprise, avec disponibilité variable selon la région AWS.
articles.title: AWS Quick now supports group assignments for custom permissions and limit profiles

articles.excerpt: AWS Quick now includes enterprise guardrails, giving administrators configurable content safety and sensitive-information controls for user prompts. Administrators can apply guardrail policies to individual users or enterprise identity provider (IdP) groups or set a policy as the account default. User-level policies take precedence over group policies and account defaults. When multiple group policies apply, Quick combines their content restrictions, using the stricter setting when controls overlap. Administrators create guardrail policies in the Quick administration console using content filters, denied topics, blocked words and phrases, prompt-attack detection, and controls for selected types of personally identifiable information (PII). For example, an administrator can create a policy that blocks prompts containing confidential project names and assign it to an IdP group. Detect-only mode lets administrators test prompt-filtering rules against real production traffic before enforcing them. In this mode, Quick evaluates user prompts and logs policy matches without blocking requests, so administrators can assess the impact on business workflows and refine policies. When administrators enable enforcement, Quick blocks matching prompts and displays a message to the user. Administrators can review detected and blocked events in Amazon CloudWatch Logs. Enterprise guardrails are available in preview for select Quick customers with Professional and Enterprise plans. For feature…
articles.summary: AWS Quick ajoute en préversion des garde-fous d'entreprise permettant aux administrateurs de configurer des contrôles de sécurité du contenu et des informations sensibles sur les requêtes des utilisateurs. Les politiques peuvent s'appliquer à un utilisateur, à un groupe de fournisseur d'identité ou comme valeur par défaut du compte, les politiques individuelles primant sur les autres. Un mode de détection seulement permet de tester les règles avant leur application, et les événements sont consignés dans Amazon CloudWatch Logs; la préversion est réservée à certains clients des forfaits Professional et Enterprise.
articles.title: AWS Quick introduces enterprise guardrails (preview)

articles.excerpt: Today, AWS announces the preview of Data Hub in AWS Billing and Cost Management, a managed data layer that enables AWS FinOps Agent to query cost and usage data with SQL. In preview, Data Hub is available to AWS FinOps Agent, so the agent can identify the individual resources behind a cost change, break down spend by team or cost allocation tag, and show how a resource's cost and usage change hour by hour. With AWS FinOps Agent and Data Hub, customers get these answers without setting up a data export or building and maintaining a cost data pipeline. Data Hub provides 13 months of hourly, resource-level cost and usage data in the published CUR 2.0 schema, including resource identifiers and cost allocation tags. AWS provisions the data, refreshes data daily, and maintains the schema as new services, commitments, and charge types are added. When set up from the management account, Data Hub covers cost and usage data across the accounts in your organization. Data Hub (preview) is available in the US East (N. Virginia) Region and covers cost and usage data across regions. There is no charge for Data Hub during preview. To learn more about Data Hub, see the AWS Billing and Cost Management User Guide and the launch blog . You can get started from the Data Hub page in the AWS Billing and Cost Management console or from the AWS FinOps Agent console.
articles.summary: AWS a lancé en préversion Data Hub dans AWS Billing and Cost Management, une couche de données gérée permettant à l'agent AWS FinOps d'interroger en SQL les données de coûts et d'utilisation. Il fournit 13 mois de données horaires au niveau des ressources, au schéma CUR 2.0, sans configuration d'exportation ni pipeline à maintenir. La préversion est disponible dans la région US East (N. Virginia), sans frais pendant cette période.
articles.title: AWS announces Data Hub in AWS Billing and Cost Management (preview)

articles.excerpt: Today, Amazon CloudWatch announces support for your own application telemetry in the CloudWatch Observability EKS add-on. The CloudWatch agent you already run now accepts metrics, traces, and logs from your applications, so you don't deploy and operate a separate collector to get them into CloudWatch. Applications instrumented with an OpenTelemetry SDK send to an OTLP endpoint that the agent serves on every node, on by default. Metrics arrive as CloudWatch metrics you query with PromQL, traces go to AWS X-Ray and Transaction Search, and logs go to CloudWatch Logs. For Prometheus metrics, the agent scrapes the targets described by standard ServiceMonitor and PodMonitor objects, with no Prometheus operator to run and no change to your scrape configuration. Each team defines its own targets alongside its application rather than in one central add-on configuration. Label selectors let you choose which monitors CloudWatch scrapes. Both sources carry the same Kubernetes, host, cloud, and service attributes the add-on applies to the pod they came from, so you can join application telemetry to your cluster metrics. Custom telemetry is available in version 8.0.0 and later of the EKS add-on and Helm chart, in all AWS Regions where CloudWatch supports OpenTelemetry metrics. Telemetry is charged at the Amazon EKS OpenTelemetry ingestion rate of $0.08 per GB. For details, see Amazon CloudWatch insights pricing . To get started, see Custom telemetry in the Amazon CloudWatch User Guide.
articles.summary: Amazon CloudWatch permet désormais à l'agent CloudWatch de l'add-on EKS Observability de recevoir la télémétrie personnalisée des applications : métriques, traces et journaux, sans collecteur séparé. Les métriques Prometheus sont extraites via les objets ServiceMonitor et PodMonitor standards, et la fonctionnalité est disponible à partir de la version 8.0.0 de l'add-on et du chart Helm, facturée 0,08 $ par Go d'ingestion.
articles.title: Amazon CloudWatch Observability EKS add-on now supports custom OpenTelemetry and Prometheus telemetry

articles.excerpt: Amazon DynamoDB vector search inline filters now support range comparisons, value lists, and logical operators in addition to the equality operator, so you can narrow a vector search to exactly the items you want. You can now filter on numeric ranges such as price, rating, or publish date, match an attribute against a list of values, check whether an attribute exists, and combine conditions with OR and NOT. Amazon DynamoDB vector indexes store vector embeddings alongside your operational data, and the SearchVectors API returns the items whose embeddings are most similar to your query vector. The search condition expression in a SearchVectors request now accepts the comparison operators <, <=, >, >=, and BETWEEN on Number attributes, the IN operator, the attribute_exists and attribute_not_exists functions, and the logical operators AND, OR, and NOT. DynamoDB applies the filter during the search, so every result it returns matches. For example, a retail application can return the products most similar to a shopper's query within a price range and a set of brands, and a retrieval-augmented generation application can limit results to selected document categories published after a given date. The new operators are available in all AWS Regions where DynamoDB vector search is available. To learn more, see vector search in the Amazon DynamoDB Developer Guide, or visit the Amazon DynamoDB page.
articles.summary: Amazon DynamoDB enrichit la recherche vectorielle de nouveaux opérateurs de filtre en ligne : comparaisons par plage, listes de valeurs, test d'existence d'attribut et opérateurs logiques OR et NOT. Ces filtres s'appliquent pendant la recherche de l'API SearchVectors, de sorte que tous les résultats renvoyés respectent la condition. Les nouveautés sont disponibles dans toutes les régions AWS où la recherche vectorielle de DynamoDB est offerte.
articles.title: Amazon DynamoDB vector search now supports new inline filter operators

articles.excerpt: Amazon Transcribe now offers a synchronous transcription API, TranscribeAudio . Send a complete audio file in a single request and get the full transcript back in the same response. There is no job to start, no status to poll, no connection to manage. The transcripts are as accurate as Amazon Transcribe batch transcription, so you can add fast, accurate speech-to-text to interactive applications such as voice assistants, agent-assist tools and on-demand "transcribe this clip" features. The synchronous API supports the Amazon Transcribe features you already use, including: Word-level timestamps and smart formatting for numbers, dates, currency and phone numbers Automatic language identification Speaker diarization, and channel identification for up to two channels Custom vocabulary and vocabulary filtering, which you can provide directly in the request with no setup step PII redaction Send audio inline (up to 25 MB) or from Amazon S3 (up to 500 MB), 0.5 seconds to 1 hour long, in WAV, MP3, FLAC, M4A, MP4, Ogg, WebM or AMR format. The transcript comes back in the response, or Transcribe can write it to an S3 location you choose. Pricing is $0.0070 per minute of audio, billed per second, with speaker diarization, language identification, custom vocabulary and channel identification included. Two-channel audio is billed once on file duration. PII redaction is available as an add-on. Supports English, Spanish, French, Italian, German, Japanese, Portuguese, Korean and Chinese…
articles.summary: Amazon Transcribe propose désormais une API de transcription synchrone, TranscribeAudio, qui renvoie la transcription complète dans la réponse à une seule requête, sans tâche ni interrogation de statut. Elle prend en charge plusieurs fonctionnalités existantes (horodatages, mise en forme intelligente, identification de la langue, diarisation des loc[…]
articles.title: Amazon Transcribe announces a synchronous transcription API

articles.excerpt: Today, Amazon CloudWatch announces telemetry filtering for the CloudWatch Observability EKS add-on, so you can stop paying to ingest telemetry you don't use. You can now set cluster-wide include and exclude lists for namespaces, metric names, and pod and node labels. Exclude the non-production namespaces you don't monitor, drop high-cardinality metrics by name, and keep only the labels you group by rather than every label on every resource. Because ingestion is billed per GB, collecting less lowers what you pay, and you can adjust filters with a single add-on configuration update as your clusters change. Telemetry filtering is available in version 8.0.0 and later of the EKS add-on and Helm chart, in all AWS Regions where CloudWatch supports OpenTelemetry metrics. Telemetry sent through the add-on is charged at the Amazon EKS OpenTelemetry ingestion rate of $0.08 per GB. For details, see Amazon CloudWatch insights pricing . To get started, see Amazon CloudWatch Observability EKS add-on in the Amazon CloudWatch User Guide .
articles.summary: Amazon CloudWatch ajoute à son module complémentaire Observability pour EKS un filtrage de télémétrie, permettant de définir des listes d'inclusion et d'exclusion par espace de noms, nom de métrique et étiquettes de pods et de nœuds afin de réduire les coûts d'ingestion. Le filtrage est disponible dans la version 8.0.0 et les suivantes, dans toutes les régions où CloudWatch prend en charge les métriques OpenTelemetry, au tarif de 0,08 $ par Go.
articles.title: Amazon CloudWatch Observability EKS add-on now supports telemetry filtering

articles.excerpt: Amazon SageMaker JumpStart now offers a model leaderboard in Amazon SageMaker Studio. You can use it to compare foundation models side by side on throughput, latency, and cost, and then deploy or customize the model that fits your workload. Comparing models has usually meant reading model cards one at a time and relying on benchmark scores that different sources published under different conditions. The JumpStart leaderboard puts consistent measurements in one view. AWS evaluates every model on three reasoning benchmarks, BIG-Bench Hard, GPQA Diamond, and MMLU-Pro, using the same evaluation setup for each model. AWS also measures time to first token, throughput, and instance cost on SageMaker for each JumpStart deployment configuration. You can use all of the filters already available for JumpStart models, such as model provider, license, and input and output modality, to narrow the list. You can also choose a use case profile and an optimization goal (balanced, cost, latency, or throughput) to see the metrics for the configuration you plan to deploy. At launch, the leaderboard covers more than 70 LLMs from providers including Meta, Google, Qwen, IBM, and Arcee. The JumpStart model leaderboard is available at no additional charge in all AWS commercial Regions where Amazon SageMaker Studio is available. To get started, open SageMaker JumpStart in SageMaker Studio and choose the Leaderboard view. To learn more, see JumpStart leaderboard methodology and read the launch blog…
articles.summary: AWS lance un classement des modèles dans SageMaker JumpStart, accessible depuis SageMaker Studio, qui permet de comparer plus de 70 LLM (Meta, Google, Qwen, IBM, Arcee, entre autres) sur le débit, la latence et le coût. Les modèles sont évalués avec une méthode uniforme sur trois benchmarks de raisonnement (BIG-Bench Hard, GPQA Diamond, MMLU-Pro), et le service est offert sans frais supplémentaires dans toutes les régions commerciales AWS où SageMaker Studio est disponible.
articles.title: Amazon SageMaker JumpStart now offers a model leaderboard to compare models on quality, speed, and cost

articles.excerpt: AWS Partner Central Agents now help AWS Partners create and manage AWS Partner Central and AWS Marketplace support cases in one place. The agents are available 24/7 and draw on Partner Central account details and authoritative, partner-specific knowledge from AWS to resolve most inquiries instantly. If a inquiry needs a support engineer, the agents will gather details and create a case. This reduces the time partners spend looking for help, and gives support teams the context they need to resolve cases faster. Partners can handle a case from start to finish in one chat, with the full record in AWS Support Center. To create a case, partners can start describing their issue to AWS Partner Central Agents or use the prompt "get support." The agents gather additional details necessary to resolve the case, set the category, and draft the description. Partners review and submit the case, and the agents route the case to the right support team. In the same chat, partners can view case communications, track progress, post replies, and add attachments. With this launch, Partner Central and AWS Marketplace cases also move to AWS Support Center. There, partners can view the full case history and translate support correspondence into Chinese, French, German, Japanese, Korean, Portuguese, and Spanish. The new support experience is available today to all AWS Partners and AWS Marketplace sellers in the AWS Partner Central console and through the AWS Partner Central Agents MCP server. With…
articles.summary: AWS a lancé des agents AWS Partner Central, disponibles 24 h sur 24, qui aident les partenaires à créer et gérer en un seul endroit leurs dossiers de support Partner Central et AWS Marketplace. Les agents résolvent la plupart des demandes immédiatement et, si un ingénieur est nécessaire, recueillent les détails et ouvrent un dossier acheminé à la bonne équipe. Les dossiers passent aussi dans AWS Support Center, où les partenaires peuvent consulter l'historique complet et traduire la correspondance dans plusieurs langues, dont le français.
articles.title: AWS Partner Central Agents now help partners create and manage Partner Central and Marketplace support cases

articles.excerpt: Builders using the new AWS experience on the Paid plan can now receive spend limit alerts by text message (SMS), alongside existing email notifications. A spend limit sets the maximum monthly cost for a project. Notifications are sent as a project approaches its limit, and when a project reaches its limit, AWS automatically pauses it. SMS gives builders a second way to stay informed about their project costs. Email alerts can go unnoticed when builders are away from their inbox, leaving little time to respond before a project is paused. SMS alerts close this gap with a text message when a project's actual costs reach 90% of its spend limit, so builders have time to act, such as raising the limit or stopping resources they don't need. To turn on SMS alerts, verify your mobile phone number in AWS Settings and turn on text alerts for spend limits. Text alerts are only sent to verified numbers, and you can opt out at any time. SMS alerts for spend limits are available at no additional charge for US phone numbers, including Puerto Rico, Guam, the US Virgin Islands, and American Samoa. To learn more, see Create a spend limit in AWS Settings , the AWS Account Management Reference Guide , or Get started with AWS .
articles.summary: AWS permet désormais d'envoyer par SMS les alertes de limite de dépenses aux utilisateurs du plan payant de la nouvelle expérience AWS, en complément des courriels. Le SMS est envoyé lorsque les coûts réels d'un projet atteignent 90 % de sa limite, afin de laisser le temps d'agir avant la mise en pause automatique du projet. Il faut vérifier son numéro de téléphone mobile dans les paramètres AWS et activer les alertes texte; le service est sans frais supplémentaires pour les numéros américains.
articles.title: Spend limits in the new AWS experience now support SMS alerts

articles.excerpt: Amazon S3 Vectors now supports up to 40 KB of filterable metadata per vector, up from 2 KB. You can attach and filter on more attributes per vector, such as category, permissions, timestamps, and descriptive tags, so your retrieval-augmented generation (RAG), agentic, and semantic-search applications can narrow results by more of the fields that matter to them. S3 Vectors provides native support to store and query vectors in Amazon S3, delivering purpose-built, cost-optimized vector storage and query at billion-vector scale. With this launch, indexes in new vector buckets support the higher limit by default, with no change to how you write vectors with PutVectors or run filtered queries with QueryVectors. To use the higher limit on an existing index, update it in place to enhanced index mode with the UpdateIndexMode API. The higher filterable metadata limit is available at no additional cost in all AWS Regions where Amazon S3 Vectors is available. To get started, use the AWS CLI, AWS SDKs, or the Amazon S3 console. To learn more, visit the Amazon S3 Vectors documentation .
articles.summary: Amazon S3 Vectors permet désormais d'associer jusqu'à 40 Ko de métadonnées filtrables par vecteur, contre 2 Ko auparavant, pour filtrer les résultats selon davantage d'attributs dans les applications RAG, agentiques et de recherche sémantique. Les nouveaux index des vector buckets bénéficient de cette limite par défaut, sans changement aux API PutVectors et QueryVectors. Les index existants peuvent y accéder en passant au mode d'index amélioré via UpdateIndexMode, sans frais supplémentaires dans toutes les régions où le service est offert.
articles.title: Amazon S3 Vectors raises the filterable metadata limit to 40 KB per vector

articles.excerpt: AWS Lambda now provides cost optimization recommendations for Event Functions in AWS Trusted Advisor . These recommendations identify on-demand functions where moving to Lambda Managed Instances (LMI) is estimated to reduce costs, and provide configuration guidance for running on LMI. With these recommendations, you can lower your Lambda costs by focusing your efforts on the functions with the greatest estimated savings. LMI lets you run Lambda functions on Amazon EC2 instances while maintaining the operational simplicity of Lambda. With LMI, you can access specialized compute configurations and drive cost efficiency through EC2 pricing options such as Savings Plans and Reserved Instances, without managing infrastructure. Previously, to determine whether a function was a good fit for LMI, you had to analyze its invocation patterns, estimate LMI costs, and select the right instance type and memory-to-vCPU ratio yourself. This manual process added overhead and delayed savings. With this launch, Lambda automatically analyzes the invocation patterns, duration, and resource utilization of your high-volume Event Functions and recommends those where LMI is estimated to reduce costs. Estimates are based on a simulation of each function's invocation patterns, using public Lambda pricing and Amazon EC2 On-Demand pricing. Each recommendation includes the function ARN, the recommended EC2 instance type and memory-to-vCPU ratio, the estimated current cost, the estimated LMI cost, and…
articles.summary: AWS Lambda propose désormais, dans AWS Trusted Advisor, des recommandations d'optimisation des coûts pour les Event Functions à forte volumétrie. Ces recommandations identifient les fonctions à la demande pour lesquelles un passage à Lambda Managed Instances (LMI) réduirait les coûts estimés, avec des conseils de configuration. Les estimations reposent sur une simulation des patterns d'invocation et sur les tarifs publics de Lambda et d'EC2 On-Demand.
articles.title: AWS Lambda now provides cost optimization recommendations for Event Functions

articles.excerpt: AWS Glue Data Catalog introduces data quality monitoring for catalogs and databases, powered by AWS Glue Data Quality, which profiles and evaluates your tables at catalog scale from a single configuration. You define data quality checks once for a catalog, a database, or a single table, and AWS Glue Data Quality evaluates every table in scope, including tables added later, on the cadence you choose. Quality issues surface as data changes, without per-table setup or manual runs, which helps keep bad data from reaching downstream consumers. You can use built-in profiling options that AWS Glue provides for common baseline statistics or provide your own Data Quality Definition Language (DQDL) ruleset with analyzers, rules, or both to hold every table in a database to the same quality standards. You have the flexibility to run evaluations once when you create the configuration or set up triggers, so evaluations run on a schedule or whenever table metadata changes, including every Apache Iceberg commit. After three runs on a table, AWS Glue Data Quality flags anomalous statistics that drift outside expected bounds, surfacing changes that no rule covers. Results are accessible through the existing AWS Glue Data Quality APIs, or you can opt-in to write them to Apache Iceberg tables in the AWS Glue Data Catalog or to Amazon S3. Data quality monitoring for catalogs and databases in AWS Glue Data Catalog is available in all AWS Commercial, AWS GovCloud (US), and AWS China regions. To…
articles.summary: AWS Glue Data Catalog ajoute une surveillance de la qualité des données à l'échelle d'un catalogue ou d'une base de données, basée sur AWS Glue Data Quality. Les règles, définies une seule fois, s'appliquent à toutes les tables concernées, y compris celles ajoutées plus tard, avec des évaluations planifiées ou déclenchées par les changements de métadonnées, dont chaque commit Apache Iceberg. Après trois exécutions, le service signale les statistiques qui sortent des bornes attendues, et les résultats sont accessibles via les API existantes ou écrits dans des tables Iceberg ou dans Amazon S3.
articles.title: AWS Glue Data Catalog introduces data quality monitoring for catalogs and databases

articles.excerpt: AWS Lambda now supports a batch size of up to 10,000 messages for Amazon Simple Queue Service (Amazon SQS) FIFO queue event source mappings (ESMs) in provisioned mode , up from 10 messages previously. With larger batches, you can process high-volume, ordered workloads such as financial transactions, order processing, and inventory updates with fewer invocations and higher throughput. Lambda continues to preserve message ordering within each message group. Customers use SQS FIFO queues with Lambda to build event-driven applications that need strict message ordering and deduplication. With provisioned mode for SQS ESMs, you can use throughput controls to set a minimum and maximum number of event pollers to meet strict performance requirements. Previously, provisioned mode customers who needed higher throughput for SQS FIFO queues were limited by the maximum batch size of 10 messages. This required them to scale out invocations or add custom buffering logic, which added operational overhead and cost. With this launch, you can set a batch size of up to 10,000 messages and a batching window of up to 300 seconds for FIFO queues, so you can process large volumes of ordered messages in fewer invocations without re-architecting your applications. This feature is available for SQS FIFO ESMs in provisioned mode in all AWS commercial Regions. You can configure the batch size and the batching window when you create new ESMs or update existing ESMs by using the Lambda console, AWS CLI…
articles.summary: AWS Lambda prend désormais en charge des lots allant jusqu'à 10 000 messages pour les files SQS FIFO en mode provisionné, contre 10 auparavant. Cela permet de traiter des charges ordonnées à fort volume avec moins d'invocations, tout en conservant l'ordre des messages dans chaque groupe. La fonctionnalité est disponible dans toutes les Régions commerciales AWS.
articles.title: AWS Lambda now supports a batch size of up to 10,000 messages for Amazon SQS FIFO queues

articles.excerpt: AWS Pricing Calculator now offers GetUsageLinesEstimatedCost, a new API that returns the estimated cost of a planned workload in a single API call. You send up to 500 usage lines in one request and get the cost back right away, without saving an estimate to your account. While workload estimates let you create and save an estimate in Pricing Calculator, GetUsageLinesEstimatedCost returns a cost on demand, directly in your own tools and workflows. You can choose from three rate types: public On-Demand rates, your rates after discounts, or your rates after discounts plus Savings Plans and Reserved Instances. The API returns the cost of each line and the total. For example, you can check what a design will cost before you deploy it, or let an AI coding agent call the API to price a workload while it helps you design it. GetUsageLinesEstimatedCost is generally available at no additional charge in all AWS Regions, except the AWS GovCloud (US) Regions and the China Regions. To learn more, see GetUsageLinesEstimatedCost in the AWS Billing and Cost Management API Reference, or visit the AWS Pricing Calculator product page .
articles.summary: AWS Pricing Calculator propose désormais l'API GetUsageLinesEstimatedCost, qui renvoie en un seul appel le coût estimé d'une charge de travail planifiée, avec jusqu'à 500 lignes d'utilisation par requête et sans enregistrer d'estimation dans le compte. Trois types de tarifs sont proposés : les tarifs publics On-Demand, les tarifs après remises, ou les tarifs après remises incluant Savings Plans et instances réservées. Elle est offerte sans frais supplémentaires dans toutes les régions AWS, sauf GovCloud (US) et les régions Chine.
articles.title: AWS Pricing Calculator now estimates workload costs through a new API

articles.excerpt: Today, AWS Billing and Cost Management announces new APIs that let you view your AWS payment information through the AWS SDKs and the AWS CLI. With these APIs, you can check your account balance, find invoices that are due or past due, see which payments and credit memos were applied to each invoice, and confirm that the payment methods on your account are active. You can call the APIs from your own tools or through an AI agent. Previously, finance teams had to sign in to the console to find past-due invoices, match payments to invoices, or check whether a payment method was still active. Now you can automate these checks with APIs such as GetFinancialRecord, BatchGetFinancialRecord, ListFinancialRecords, GetAccountBalance, GetPaymentInstrument and ListPaymentInstruments. You can integrate the APIs with your accounts payable systems to monitor past-due balances and reconcile AWS invoices on your own schedule. The APIs are available in the US East (N. Virginia) Region, and available to customers in all commercial AWS Regions. To learn more, visit the AWS Payments API Reference .
articles.summary: AWS Billing and Cost Management lance de nouvelles API, accessibles via les SDK AWS et l'AWS CLI, pour consulter les informations de paiement d'un compte : solde, factures échues ou à échéance, paiements et notes de crédit appliqués, et état des moyens de paiement. Ces API permettent d'automatiser ces vérifications, y compris depuis un agent IA, et de les intégrer aux systèmes de comptes fournisseurs. Elles sont offertes dans toutes les régions commerciales AWS.
articles.title: AWS Billing and Cost Management now offers APIs to track payment status

articles.excerpt: Amazon EventBridge Scheduler expands its AWS SDK integrations with 589 new API actions across 81 AWS services, and adds templated targets for the enhanced EventBridge Custom event bus. You can now schedule direct invocations of a broader set of AWS services without writing custom integration code. EventBridge Scheduler is a serverless scheduler that allows you to create, run, and manage billions of scheduled events and tasks across more than 270 AWS services, without provisioning or managing the underlying infrastructure. With a new templated target, you can schedule event delivery directly to the Custom event bus using its PutEvents or PutRawEvents API. The templated target also makes it easier to add metadata fields to each event. For example, you can send an event to your bus every night at midnight to start a reconciliation workflow, with no function in between to call the API. The new API actions are available in all commercial AWS Regions where Amazon EventBridge Scheduler is available, subject to the availability of each target service in the Region. The templated targets for the Custom event bus are available in all AWS Regions where the enhanced Custom event bus is available. To learn more, see Using templated targets in EventBridge Scheduler and Using universal targets in EventBridge Scheduler in the Amazon EventBridge Scheduler User Guide. Install the Agent Toolkit for AWS to start building with your AI coding agent.
articles.summary: Amazon EventBridge Scheduler ajoute 589 nouvelles actions d'API provenant de 81 services AWS, ce qui permet de planifier des invocations directes sans code d'intégration personnalisé. Une nouvelle cible templatisée permet aussi d'envoyer des événements planifiés directement au bus d'événements personnalisé via PutEvents ou PutRawEvents, avec ajout facile de métadonnées.
articles.title: Amazon EventBridge Scheduler adds 589 new API actions and event bus targets

articles.excerpt: Amazon EventBridge now supports Webhook Events for the enhanced Custom event bus, so SaaS applications, AI agents, and custom integrations can send events to a bus over HTTPS. You no longer need to deploy and operate your own API endpoint and compute to receive webhooks and publish them to your bus. The EventBridge Custom event bus is a serverless event broker that enables you to create scalable event-driven applications by routing events between your applications, SaaS integrations, and AWS services. When you create a webhook event source on your bus, EventBridge provides a managed HTTPS URL and verifies each request using an HMAC signature, a static token, or basic authentication. EventBridge then publishes accepted events to the bus, where Subscribers filter and deliver them like any other event. For example, shipment status updates from a logistics partner can reach your order tracking and customer notification Subscribers as soon as the partner sends them. Webhook Events are available in all AWS Regions where the enhanced Custom event bus is available. Events received through a webhook are billed as standard Custom event bus ingress, with no additional charge for the webhook. To learn more, see Webhook Events in the Amazon EventBridge User Guide and the Amazon EventBridge product page . Install the Agent Toolkit for AWS to start building with your AI coding agent.
articles.summary: Amazon EventBridge permet désormais de recevoir des événements par webhook sur son bus Custom enrichi, ce qui permet aux applications SaaS, aux agents IA et aux intégrations personnalisées d'envoyer des événements en HTTPS sans avoir à déployer leur propre point d'accès. EventBridge fournit une URL HTTPS gérée et vérifie les requêtes par signature HMAC, jeton statique ou authentification de base. Les événements acceptés sont publiés sur le bus et facturés comme une ingestion Custom event bus standard, sans frais supplémentaires pour le webhook.
articles.title: Amazon EventBridge Custom event bus now supports Webhook Events

articles.excerpt: Amazon EventBridge now supports Amazon Managed Streaming for Apache Kafka (Amazon MSK) as a target for the enhanced Custom event bus, so you can deliver events to Kafka topics without running your own producer. The EventBridge Custom event bus is a serverless event broker that enables you to create scalable event-driven applications by routing events between your applications, SaaS integrations, and AWS services. To deliver events to MSK, you create a Subscriber that specifies the cluster ARN and topic. You can also configure Kafka producer settings such as partition key, acknowledgment level, and record headers. EventBridge supports both public and private, serverless and provisioned clusters. When you create a Subscriber for a private cluster, EventBridge automatically sets up a private connection to the cluster. For example, teams that publish to a shared Custom event bus can now deliver purchase-order events to the MSK topics their payments team already consumes from. Amazon MSK targets are available in all AWS Regions where the enhanced Custom event bus is available. Delivery to MSK is billed as standard Custom event bus egress. EventBridge also supports compression before delivery, which is billed as an Event Evaluation. To learn more, see Amazon MSK cluster target in the Amazon EventBridge User Guide and the Amazon EventBridge product page . Install the Agent Toolkit for AWS to start building with your AI coding agent.
articles.summary: Amazon EventBridge peut désormais livrer des événements directement à des topics Amazon MSK (Kafka) depuis son bus d'événements personnalisé amélioré, sans producteur Kafka à exploiter soi-même. La configuration se fait par un abonné précisant l'ARN du cluster et le topic, avec des réglages comme la clé de partition, le niveau d'accusé de réception et les en-têtes de records; les clusters publics et privés, serverless et provisionnés, sont pris en charge. La fonctionnalité est offerte dans toutes les régions où le bus amélioré est disponible, avec facturation comme sortie standard du bus.
articles.title: Amazon EventBridge Custom event bus now supports Amazon MSK as a target

articles.excerpt: Amazon Connect Customer enhances service level agreements (SLAs) for cases, so teams can set service goals for more of their work and respond faster when a case falls behind. Admins can set SLAs on case fields beyond status, such as requiring a case’s severity to drop from high to medium within 24 hours. Admins can add an email action to SLA breach rules, so the assigned agent learns right away when a case misses its SLA. Developers can use APIs to adjust a case’s SLA deadline when the team is waiting on information from an outside party, such as a partner. Cases is available in the following AWS Regions: US East (N. Virginia), US West (Oregon), Canada (Central), Europe (Frankfurt), Europe (London), Asia Pacific (Seoul), Asia Pacific (Singapore), Asia Pacific (Sydney), Asia Pacific (Tokyo), and Africa (Cape Town). To learn more and get started, visit the Cases webpage and documentation .
articles.summary: Amazon Connect Customer permet désormais de définir des accords de niveau de service (SLA) sur d'autres champs de dossier que le statut, par exemple exiger qu'une gravité passe de élevée à moyenne en 24 heures. Les administrateurs peuvent ajouter une action courriel aux règles de bris de SLA, et les développeurs peuvent ajuster l'échéance via des API lorsqu'une équipe attend une information d'un tiers.
articles.title: Amazon Connect Customer expands how teams track and act on service level agreements for cases

articles.excerpt: Amazon Managed Streaming for Apache Kafka (Amazon MSK) now supports Apache Kafka version 4.2 on Standard brokers. A key highlight of this release is Queues for Kafka, which is now production ready. With Queues, multiple consumers can process messages from the same topic partitions, which improves parallelism and throughput for workloads that need point-to-point message delivery. This release also includes Eligible Leader Replicas (ELR) enhancements that improve leader election correctness and strengthen availability. The new consumer rebalance protocol makes consumer group rebalances smoother and faster. The new Streams Rebalance Protocol extends broker-side coordination to Kafka Streams applications so tasks get assigned more efficiently. For the full list of improvements and bug fixes, see the Apache Kafka 4.2 release notes . To start using Apache Kafka 4.2 on Amazon MSK, select version 4.2.x when creating a new cluster with the AWS Management Console, AWS CLI, or AWS SDKs. You can also upgrade existing MSK provisioned clusters with an in-place rolling update. Amazon MSK orchestrates broker restarts to maintain availability and protect your data during the upgrade. Kafka version 4.2 support is available today in all AWS regions where Amazon MSK Standard brokers is offered. To learn how to get started, see the Amazon MSK Developer Guide .
articles.summary: Amazon MSK prend désormais en charge Apache Kafka 4.2 sur ses courtiers Standard, avec Queues for Kafka maintenant prêt pour la production, permettant à plusieurs consommateurs de traiter les messages d'une même partition de topic. La version ajoute aussi des améliorations de l'élection de leader (ELR), un nouveau protocole de rééquilibrage des consommateurs et un protocole de rééquilibrage pour Kafka Streams, et peut être déployée sur de nouveaux clusters ou via une mise à jour progressive des clusters existants dans toutes les régions AWS où MSK Standard est offert.
articles.title: Amazon MSK Standard Brokers adds support for Apache Kafka version 4.2

articles.excerpt: Amazon Elastic Container Service (Amazon ECS) now extends Action Logs to include tasks, container instances, clusters, and capacity providers, so you can see why your tasks failed or why your clusters didn't scale as desired. Action Logs provide detailed, timestamped records of the actions Amazon ECS performs on your behalf, and until now covered service deployments and managed daemon updates. With the expanded coverage, you can diagnose task failures and scaling issues yourself, and resolve them faster than before, without contacting AWS support. If you use Action Logs already, you receive the new events automatically with no configuration changes. When a task fails to start, Action Logs show the reason. Examples include image pull failures, missing permissions for Amazon EBS volumes, or lack of available IP addresses in the subnet. When a running task stops, you can see the container exit code and the health check that triggered the stop. For cluster infrastructure, Action Logs record container instance registration and draining, Amazon EC2 instances that fail to register with a cluster, capacity provider changes, and managed scaling actions, including when an Amazon EC2 Auto Scaling group reaches its maximum size. Each log entry includes the event name, log level (INFO, WARN, or ERROR), relevant resource ARNs, and a status reason. Action Logs is available in AWS Regions, including the AWS GovCloud (US) Regions . You can opt in at the cluster level through the Amazon ECS…
articles.summary: Amazon ECS étend ses Action Logs aux tâches, aux instances de conteneurs, aux clusters et aux fournisseurs de capacité, ce qui permet de voir pourquoi une tâche échoue ou pourquoi un cluster ne se met pas à l'échelle. Les journaux couvrent par exemple les échecs de téléchargement d'image, les permissions manquantes pour les volumes EBS ou le manque d'adresses IP dans le sous-réseau. Les utilisateurs existants reçoivent ces nouveaux événements automatiquement, sans modification de configuration.
articles.title: Amazon ECS Action Logs now cover tasks, container instances, and capacity providers

articles.excerpt: Today, AWS announced the general availability of third-party UI component porting for ASP.NET web site modernization in AWS Transform. When AWS Transform modernizes a legacy ASP.NET web site, it now detects dependencies on popular third-party UI component libraries. You can replace them with license-free Microsoft-native and open-source components, or you can keep using vendor UI libraries. AWS Transform rewrites legacy ASP.NET web sites for ASP.NET Core UI frameworks. When the AWS Transform for .NET modernization agent finds a dependency on a popular third-party UI library, it offers two options. The first option is for customers who require open-source software only. The agent replaces each proprietary control with a Microsoft-native or open-source control on the target UI framework and removes the original dependency. The second option is for customers who want to keep using vendor libraries. The agent adds code comments and next-step instructions for moving to an equivalent vendor library on the target UI framework. You then arrange licensing with the vendor and finish the port using an AI coding companion. This capability is available at no additional cost in all eight AWS Regions where AWS Transform is offered: US East (N. Virginia), Canada (Central), Asia Pacific (Mumbai), Asia Pacific (Seoul), Asia Pacific (Sydney), Asia Pacific (Tokyo), Europe (Frankfurt), and Europe (London). To learn more, see Porting UI layer code in the AWS Transform User Guide.
articles.summary: AWS a annoncé la disponibilité générale du portage des composants d'interface tiers pour la modernisation de sites ASP.NET dans AWS Transform. Lorsqu'une dépendance à une bibliothèque d'interface populaire est détectée, l'utilisateur peut la remplacer par des composants Microsoft ou open source sans licence, ou conserver la bibliothèque du fournisseur avec des instructions pour la migrer. La fonctionnalité est offerte sans frais supplémentaires dans les huit régions où AWS Transform est disponible.
articles.title: AWS Transform announces UI component modernization for Windows web applications

articles.excerpt: AWS Lambda MicroVMs is now available in 7 additional AWS Regions: Asia Pacific (Osaka), Asia Pacific (Seoul), Canada (Central), Europe (London), Europe (Paris), South America (São Paulo), and US West (N. California). With this launch, you can use Lambda MicroVMs in a total of 21 AWS Regions. Lambda MicroVMs is a serverless compute primitive that provides VM-level isolation, near-instant launch and resume speeds, and state preservation for executing user or AI generated code. The service enables secure, stateful, and responsive code execution for applications including AI coding assistants, interactive development environments, and vulnerability scanners. With today's launch, developers can run Lambda MicroVMs closer to their end-users in 7 additional Regions, helping meet latency and data residency requirements. To get started, create a MicroVM image from your Dockerfile, then launch MicroVMs from that image. Give each user or job their own MicroVM with a dedicated HTTPS URL that supports popular connectivity protocols such as HTTP/2, gRPC, and WebSockets. You can use MicroVMs through the AWS Lambda console, AWS CloudFormation, AWS Cloud Development Kit, or with your preferred Agentic development tools using the Agent Toolkit for AWS . To learn more, visit the AWS Lambda MicroVMs developer guide . For information on pricing, see Lambda MicroVMs pricing . Visit the AWS Capabilities by Region page for the latest region availability.
articles.summary: AWS Lambda MicroVMs est désormais disponible dans 7 régions AWS supplémentaires, dont Canada (Centre), Europe (Londres), Europe (Paris), Asie-Pacifique (Osaka et Séoul), Amérique du Sud (São Paulo) et US West (N. California), portant le total à 21 régions. Ce service de calcul sans serveur offre une isolation au niveau de la machine virtuelle et des temps de lancement quasi instantanés pour exécuter du code généré par des utilisateurs ou par l'IA. Il permet de rapprocher l'exécution des utilisateurs finaux, ce qui aide à répondre aux exigences de latence et de résidence des données.
articles.title: AWS Lambda MicroVMs is now available in 7 additional AWS regions

articles.excerpt: Amazon Managed Service for Prometheus now supports up to 2 billion active metric time series and up to 300,000 total recording and alerting rules per workspace. Customers can also create multiple workspaces per account. This lets them store and analyze billions of Prometheus metrics across their organization. Amazon Managed Service for Prometheus is a fully managed, Prometheus-compatible monitoring service. It helps you monitor and alert on operational metrics at scale. It scales ingestion and storage automatically for high-cardinality workloads across containerized, serverless and hybrid environments. To get started, create an Amazon Managed Service for Prometheus workspace. To raise your active series or rules limits, file a service limit increase request in AWS Support Center or AWS Service Quotas. To learn more, see the Amazon Managed Service for Prometheus user guide and the product page.
articles.summary: Amazon Managed Service for Prometheus prend désormais en charge jusqu'à 2 milliards de séries temporelles actives et jusqu'à 300 000 règles d'enregistrement et d'alerte par espace de travail. Les clients peuvent aussi créer plusieurs espaces de travail par compte. Pour augmenter ces limites, il faut soumettre une demande via AWS Support Center ou AWS Service Quotas.
articles.title: Amazon Managed Service for Prometheus supports 2B active metrics and 300K rules per workspace

articles.excerpt: You can now upgrade existing Amazon MSK Provisioned clusters from Standard brokers to Express brokers in place, with fully managed data migration and no application changes. Express brokers are designed to deliver up to 3x more throughput per broker, scale up to 20x faster, and recover up to 90% faster compared to Standard brokers. With in-place upgrade, you can get the performance and operational benefits of Express brokers in hours, without needing to create a new cluster or having to migrate your data and applications to it. The upgrade keeps cluster endpoints unchanged, eliminating application cutovers, and preserves consumer offsets, so stateful applications such as Apache Flink and Kafka Streams continue without reprocessing or duplicates. Express brokers make Apache Kafka simpler to manage and more cost-effective to run at scale, with pay-as-you-go storage that scales automatically and built-in best practice defaults for higher resilience. Previously, upgrading to Express brokers meant creating a new cluster and migrating workloads to it, which required careful planning and cross-team coordination. With this launch, you can upgrade your existing Standard brokers to Express brokers in-place, without interrupting your applications, while maintaining complete control over the upgrade process. The upgrade adds Express brokers to your cluster and moves your topics to them, either automatically or in batches you control. Your Standard brokers stay in the cluster until you…
articles.summary: Amazon MSK permet désormais de mettre à niveau en place un cluster Provisioned existant, des brokers Standard vers des brokers Express, avec migration des données entièrement gérée et sans modification des applications. Selon AWS, les brokers Express offrent jusqu'à trois fois plus de débit par broker, une mise à l'échelle jusqu'à 20 fois plus rapide et une reprise jusqu'à 90 % plus rapide, les points de terminaison du cluster et les décalages des consommateurs étant conservés.
articles.title: Amazon MSK now supports in-place upgrade from Standard brokers to Express brokers

articles.excerpt: Amazon Managed Service for Prometheus is now available in the AWS European Sovereign Cloud (Germany) region, along with Amazon Managed Service for Prometheus collector. Amazon Managed Service for Prometheus is a fully managed, Prometheus-compatible monitoring service, that helps you monitor and alert on operational metrics at scale. Customers in the AWS European Sovereign Cloud can now run Prometheus-compatible monitoring workloads in-region, which lowers latency for local workloads and keeps metric data within the region. Amazon Managed Service for Prometheus collector is a fully managed, agentless collector. It discovers and collects Prometheus metrics from your container workloads, so you do not need to run collection agents yourself. The collector sends metrics to an Amazon Managed Service for Prometheus workspace, where you query and analyze them. A workspace is a logical space for storing and querying Prometheus metrics. For the full list of regions where Amazon Managed Service for Prometheus is available, see the AWS Regional Services List . For pricing, see the Amazon Managed Service for Prometheus pricing page . To learn more, see the Amazon Managed Service for Prometheus user guide and the product page.
articles.summary: Amazon Managed Service for Prometheus, ainsi que son collecteur géré, est désormais disponible dans la région AWS European Sovereign Cloud (Allemagne). Les clients peuvent ainsi exécuter leurs charges de surveillance compatibles Prometheus dans la région, ce qui réduit la latence et conserve les données de métriques sur place. Le collecteur, sans agent, récupère les métriques des charges de conteneurs et les envoie vers un espace de travail pour les interroger.
articles.title: Amazon Managed Service for Prometheus now available in the AWS European Sovereign Cloud (Germany) region

articles.excerpt: AWS Lambda now supports creating serverless applications using Node.js 26, for both Lambda Web Functions and Lambda Event Functions. Developers can use Node.js 26 as both a managed runtime and a base container image (Event Functions only). AWS will automatically apply updates to the managed runtime and base image as they become available. Node.js 26 is the latest long-term support release of Node.js and is expected to be supported for security and bug fixes until April 2029. With this release, you can use the latest Node.js 26 features in Lambda, such as the Temporal API for easier date, time, and time zone handling, and enhancements to the Fetch API.
